title: Should Remote Work Expand?
text:
Source A - Expand with Training
A six-month remote-work pilot included 200 employees. Completed projects rose 12 percent and average sick days fell. Seventy-eight percent of participants preferred the flexible schedule. Managers reported some communication delays, so the company recommends training managers and requiring two shared office days before expanding the policy.

Source B - Return to the Office
A department manager argues that remote work should end because employees may become distracted at home and teamwork could weaken. He says face-to-face communication feels more productive and predicts that performance will decline if the policy expands. He provides no productivity data from the pilot and does not compare the pilot group with office-only employees.
